versions.question: Arrange the steps for baking a golden image that new instances can boot from.
items: Start an instance from a base AMI and install your software
Shut the instance down so the disk is quiescent
Run create-image on the stopped instance, which snapshots its EBS volumes
Start fresh instances from the new image in whichever AZ you need
versions.explanation: Stopping avoids capturing a half-written file system; registering the AMI snapshots the volumes, and the AMI can be launched in any AZ of its Region.

versions.question: After you register a custom AMI from an EBS-backed instance, what does AWS keep behind the scenes to back it?
options: A compressed copy of the instance's RAM stored in S3
EBS snapshots of the instance's volumes
A CloudFormation template describing the instance's network setup
A shared EFS volume mounted read-only by each launch
versions.explanation: An AMI of an EBS-backed instance references EBS snapshots of its volumes; stopping first keeps the file system consistent.

versions.question: For the object `s3://logs-archive/app/2026/09/errors.log`, which string is the S3 object key?
options: logs-archive
logs-archive/app/2026/09/errors.log
app/2026/09/errors.log
errors.log
versions.explanation: The key is everything after the bucket name: the prefix `app/2026/09/` plus the object name `errors.log`.

versions.question: In the S3 console, a 'folder' named `photos/2026/` contains `cat.jpg`. What is that folder really?
options: A directory object that holds cat.jpg and carries its own ACL
A sub-bucket created beneath the parent bucket
A key prefix that is simply part of the key `photos/2026/cat.jpg`
A mount point that S3 creates when folder view is switched on
versions.explanation: S3 is flat; the key is prefix + object name and the console just renders slashes as folders.

versions.question: You create a brand-new custom network ACL in a VPC and have not edited it yet. How does it behave compared with the VPC's default NACL?
options: Both permit all traffic because security groups handle all of the filtering instead of NACLs
The custom NACL permits everything while the default NACL blocks all traffic
Both block all traffic until an explicit allow rule is created in each of them
The custom NACL blocks everything until rules are added; the default permits all traffic
versions.explanation: The default NACL has allow-all rules; a newly created custom NACL denies everything until you add rules.

versions.question: Why can you usually ignore NACLs when working only in the default VPC?
options: Its default NACL already allows all inbound and outbound traffic
Default VPC subnets are not associated with any network ACL at all
Its default NACL is stateful and tracks each connection for you
NACL rules only apply to traffic that leaves the Region
versions.explanation: The default NACL permits all traffic, whereas a custom one starts as deny-all.

versions.question: Which three things does an EC2 Auto Scaling group do for you? (Choose three)
options: Terminates and replaces an instance that fails its health check
Adds newly launched instances as targets of a linked load balancer
Can treat a failed load balancer health check as grounds to replace an instance
Bills an extra per-hour management fee for each group created
Rebuilds the AMI with the latest OS updates on running instances
Moves running instances between Regions to balance load
versions.explanation: ASGs keep capacity by replacing unhealthy instances, register instances with the ELB and can use ELB health checks. There is no charge for the ASG itself.

versions.question: A team wants a self-healing web tier. Which three behaviours of an Auto Scaling group help? (Choose three)
options: Maintains the desired instance count after an instance dies
Automatically attaches launched instances to the target group
Can use the ALB's health verdict rather than only EC2 status checks
Resizes the instance type of running servers to fit demand
Applies OS security patches in place without relaunching
Replicates the database layer to a second Region
versions.explanation: Self-healing comes from health checks plus replacement, with load balancer integration for registration and health reporting.

versions.question: An app receives ThrottlingException errors, and separately cannot create an 11th VPC in a Region. Which two limit categories do these represent? (Choose two)
options: Request rate limits on API calls
Service quotas on the number of resources
Per-user IAM data-transfer caps
Contractual SLA credit thresholds
Billing alarms set on the account
versions.explanation: Rate limits cause throttling; quotas cap how many resources you can create (many can be raised on request).

versions.question: Which two kinds of limits does AWS apply to your usage? (Choose two)
options: A ceiling on the requests per second you may send to an API
A ceiling on how many resources of a type you can have in a Region
A fixed monthly data-transfer ceiling set per IAM role
Limits that only apply to the root user
A hard cap that support can never raise
versions.explanation: Throttling comes from API request limits; quota errors come from resource-count limits.

versions.question: A security team wants CloudFront viewer-request data within seconds so a consumer can react to 5xx spikes. Where should the real-time logs be sent?
options: Amazon S3 as standard access logs, which are delivered in batches
AWS CloudTrail trails with data events enabled for the distribution
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, as a stream
CloudWatch Alarms attached directly to the distribution's origin
versions.explanation: Real-time logs go to Kinesis Data Streams within seconds; standard logs go to S3 and are delayed.

versions.question: Which CloudFront logging option is cheapest for months of batch queries with Athena when delivery latency does not matter?
options: Real-time logs in Kinesis Data Streams at full sampling
Standard access logs written to an S3 bucket
Logs kept in a local file on each edge for later download
CloudTrail management events recorded for the distribution
versions.explanation: Standard logs land in S3, cheap and well suited to Athena; real-time logs use Kinesis for second-level latency.

versions.question: Which Route 53 routing policy would you use to return several healthy IP addresses in one response, and what is its cap per query?
options: Weighted routing, which returns all records in the set
Multi-value answer, up to 8 healthy records
Failover routing, up to 2 records
Simple routing, up to 16 records
versions.explanation: Multi-value answer returns up to eight healthy records chosen at random.

versions.question: A name has 20 multi-value answer records, all passing health checks. How many does Route 53 place in one response?
options: All 20, in weight order
Only one, as in simple routing
Up to 16, split across two answers
Up to 8, chosen at random
versions.explanation: The cap is eight healthy records per query.

versions.question: Users report that opening your EC2-hosted site just hangs until the browser gives up. Which is the first thing to check?
options: Whether the application process crashed and is returning connection refused errors
Whether the instance profile has the right managed policy attached to it
Whether the security group has an inbound rule for the web port
Whether the user data script is idempotent when the instance reboots
versions.explanation: A timeout points to blocked network traffic (security group, NACL); connection refused means the host answered but nothing listens.

versions.question: Connecting to an EC2 web server returns 'connection refused' immediately rather than timing out. What does this suggest?
options: A security group is silently dropping the packets before they arrive
The route table has no route to the internet gateway for this subnet
The network path is open but nothing is listening on that port
The instance's IAM role is missing a permission needed for inbound traffic
versions.explanation: Refused means the packet reached the host and was rejected; timeouts indicate firewall or routing problems.

versions.question: Which pipeline delivers CloudFront real-time logs for processing and onward storage?
options: An SQS FIFO queue feeding an RDS table
A CloudWatch Logs agent installed on every edge location
S3 Event Notifications that fire on each viewer request
Kinesis Data Streams, optionally consumed by Firehose
versions.explanation: Real-time logs are pushed to a Kinesis data stream, with configurable fields, sampling rate and cache behaviors.

versions.question: Which three settings can you choose on a CloudFront real-time log configuration? (Choose three)
options: The sampling rate of requests
The set of log fields to include
The cache behaviors to which it applies
The IAM user who owns each log line
The EBS volume type used to buffer logs
The Availability Zones that process the logs
versions.explanation: Real-time log configs let you choose sampling rate, fields and cache behaviors; delivery is to Kinesis Data Streams.

versions.question: Which statement best describes the EFS Max I/O performance mode?
options: It gives the lowest per-operation latency, ideal for small web-serving workloads
It scales to higher aggregate throughput and IOPS for highly parallel clients, at the cost of somewhat higher latency
It lets you pay for throughput independent of the amount of data stored
It stores data in a single AZ to reduce cost
versions.explanation: Max I/O is built for highly parallel workloads and trades latency for scale. Throughput modes and One Zone storage are separate settings.

versions.question: A CMS used by a few dozen instances needs the lowest per-operation latency from EFS. Which performance mode should be chosen at creation?
options: Max I/O
General Purpose
Provisioned
One Zone
versions.explanation: General Purpose is the default and gives the lowest latency; Max I/O trades latency for scale. Provisioned is a throughput mode and One Zone is a storage option.

versions.question: Which three workloads is Amazon S3 well suited for? (Choose three)
options: Hosting a static website's HTML and images
Keeping long-term copies of data for backup and recovery
Storing raw files for a big data lake
Running a transactional PostgreSQL engine
Serving as the boot disk of an EC2 instance
Providing low-latency POSIX file locking
versions.explanation: S3 is scalable object storage used for backup, static hosting and data lakes, not for databases or block volumes.

versions.question: A team lists ideas for Amazon S3. Which three are appropriate? (Choose three)
options: Archiving old compliance records cheaply
Storing the input files for an Athena analytics pipeline
Serving images and videos to a website
Mounting it as the root device of a Linux server
Running an Oracle database on it
Using it as an in-memory cache
versions.explanation: Object storage fits archive, analytics and media hosting; databases and boot volumes need block storage.

versions.question: A company must keep a copy of its S3 data in a different Region to satisfy a regulator. Which S3 capability does this automatically?
options: S3 Transfer Acceleration enabled through a second Regional endpoint of the bucket
Object Lock in governance mode on the source bucket
S3 Select run against the source bucket with a filter
Cross-Region replication, with versioning on both buckets
versions.explanation: CRR asynchronously copies new objects to a bucket in another Region; both buckets need versioning.

versions.question: Which prerequisite is required to configure S3 replication between two buckets?
options: Versioning enabled on both source and destination
Both buckets must use the Glacier storage class
Both buckets must sit in the same account and Region
Static website hosting enabled on both buckets
versions.explanation: Replication needs versioning on both buckets plus an IAM role allowing S3 to read and write.

versions.question: An Auto Scaling group is created with minimum 1, desired 3 and maximum 5. How many instances are running once it has finished launching?
options: One, the minimum, until demand rises
Five, the maximum, to be safe
Three, matching desired capacity
None until a scaling policy fires an action
versions.explanation: The group launches to desired capacity, which sits between min and max.

versions.question: What determines how many instances an Auto Scaling group tries to run at any moment?
options: Always the maximum size configured on the group, which it launches immediately
Always the minimum size unless an alarm is firing
The number of Availability Zones multiplied by two
Its desired capacity, within the min and max limits
versions.explanation: Scaling policies move desired capacity within the min/max limits.

versions.question: A distribution serves images and a JSON API. Which setup raises the cache hit ratio the most?
options: One default behavior forwarding every cookie and header to the origin for all paths
A TTL of zero on every path so content is always fresh at the edge
Separate behaviors, with a minimal image cache key and an API key limited to needed values
A full invalidation scheduled every hour to keep the cache small
versions.explanation: Forwarding fewer values in the cache key means more requests share a cached object; use separate cache policies per content type.

versions.question: Which practice reduces cache-key fragmentation in CloudFront?
options: Forward every request header so the origin sees the whole request
Append a random query string to each request for uniqueness
Include only the headers, cookies and query strings that change the response
Create one distribution per file extension and cache nothing
versions.explanation: Smaller cache keys mean more requests hit the same cached object.

versions.question: Which three advantages does Amazon RDS offer over a self-managed MySQL on EC2? (Choose three)
options: OS and engine patching handled during maintenance windows
Automated backups that allow restoring to a specific second
Easy Multi-AZ standby and read replica setup
Root shell access to tune the host kernel
Ability to install custom agents on the database server
Unlimited free storage
versions.explanation: RDS manages patching, backups and HA; the trade-off is no host SSH.

versions.question: A team prefers not to administer database servers. Which three RDS features support that? (Choose three)
options: Instances are provisioned and configured automatically
Point-in-time recovery from continuous backups
Read replicas can be added with a few clicks
Direct SSH login for installing OS packages
Choice of any custom kernel version
Billing only for queries executed
versions.explanation: RDS is a managed service, so you give up host access but gain automation.

versions.question: A role's IAM policy lacks s3:GetObject, but the bucket policy in the same account allows that role to read, with no Deny statements. What is the result?
options: Denied, since both policies must allow it
Denied, since the object also needs a matching ACL grant
The read is allowed, because one Allow is enough
Denied, since access can only come from a different account
versions.explanation: In the same account, an Allow in either policy suffices unless an explicit Deny exists.

versions.question: Which element always overrides every other permission during S3 policy evaluation?
options: An Allow in a bucket policy
An explicit Deny statement
An Allow attached to the account's root user
A public-read object ACL
versions.explanation: Explicit Deny wins; otherwise any applicable Allow suffices; default is deny.

versions.question: A VPC-attached Lambda in a private subnet can query its database but calls to an external SaaS endpoint time out. What fixes this?
options: Assign an Elastic IP address to the function so it has a public address
Raise the function timeout to the 15 minute maximum allowed
Route the private subnet's 0.0.0.0/0 traffic to a NAT Gateway in a public subnet
Attach an internet gateway to the function's own configuration
versions.explanation: VPC Lambdas have no public IPs, so internet egress needs NAT.

versions.question: How does a Lambda function configured with VPC subnets reach the internet?
options: Always through the Lambda service network, regardless of subnet
Directly via an internet gateway attached to the VPC, even from private subnets
It is given a public IP address automatically at each invoke, then released afterward
Through its subnet's route table, so private subnets need a NAT Gateway
versions.explanation: Lambda ENIs only get private IPs, so a NAT Gateway or VPC endpoints are required.

versions.question: A newly hired admin has the AdministratorAccess policy yet the Billing console says access denied. What must be done?
options: Attach the Billing managed policy from the Organizations console to the admin
The account owner must switch on billing visibility for IAM principals
Switch the console to us-east-1 and retry the page
Turn on CloudTrail for the account so billing pages unlock
versions.explanation: The root user must activate IAM access to billing; it is off by default.

versions.question: Who can activate IAM access to the Billing console?
options: Any IAM user who has the AdministratorAccess policy
Anyone who can assume the Organizations management role
Only the account's root user, through account settings
AWS Support, on request from an administrator
versions.explanation: Even administrators are blocked until the root user flips that account setting.

versions.question: Which rule best lets an auto-scaling web tier connect to PostgreSQL while keeping the database protected?
options: Inbound 5432 from the entire VPC CIDR block of the network
Inbound TCP 5432 on the DB group, sourced from the web tier's group
Inbound 5432 from a list of public IPs that is edited by hand
Inbound on all ports from 0.0.0.0/0, relying on strong credentials
versions.explanation: Referencing a security group follows instances as they scale.

versions.question: Why reference a security group instead of IP addresses as a rule source?
options: Security group references are free but IP rules are billed hourly
IP-based rules only work for outbound traffic, never inbound
Instances joining that group are covered with no rule edits
Security groups cannot contain CIDR ranges at all
versions.explanation: Group-referencing rules handle dynamic IPs.

versions.question: One HTTPS listener on an ALB needs to present different certificates for several domain names. Which feature enables it?
options: SNI, picking the certificate from the hostname
Connection draining configured on each target group
Path-based routing rules defined on the listener
Spreading requests evenly over targets in every AZ
versions.explanation: ALB supports multiple certificates per listener via SNI.

versions.question: Which services support SNI so that one endpoint can serve several TLS certificates? (Choose two)
options: Application Load Balancer
Classic Load Balancer
Amazon CloudFront
Gateway Load Balancer
versions.explanation: SNI works on ALB, NLB and CloudFront; the Classic LB supports only one certificate.

versions.question: Objects are replicated from bucket X to Y, and Y is configured to replicate to Z. What happens to objects that originated in X?
options: They are copied on to Z as well
They reach Z only if Y uses a different storage class
They reach Y only; they are not forwarded on to Z
They reach Z only after versioning is suspended
versions.explanation: Replication is not transitive; configure X to Z directly if needed.

versions.question: How do you get objects from one source bucket into two destination buckets with S3 replication?
options: Replicate to the first destination and let it chain onward to the second
Enable Transfer Acceleration on all three buckets so the copies chain faster
Create a separate replication rule from the source to each destination
Use a lifecycle rule on the first destination to forward objects
versions.explanation: There is no replication chaining.

versions.question: For `s3://assets/images/2026/logo.png`, which part is the prefix?
options: assets/
logo.png
images/2026/
assets/images/
versions.explanation: The prefix is the key minus the object name.

versions.question: S3 request-rate limits apply per prefix, so throughput scales best when you do what?
options: Keep every object under one single long prefix
Spread objects across many different prefixes
Turn on versioning for the bucket
Store one very large object per bucket
versions.explanation: Request limits apply per prefix, so more prefixes raises aggregate throughput.

versions.question: Which three ways can an S3 object end up in a different storage class? (Choose three)
options: Specify the class in the upload request
Copy the object over itself with a new class
A lifecycle transition rule
Turning on bucket logging
Enabling MFA Delete
Creating an access point
versions.explanation: Classes can be set on upload, changed manually and automated with lifecycle.

versions.question: Which three would change or set an object's storage class? (Choose three)
options: PUT with a storage-class header
Manual change in the console
Lifecycle configuration
Static website hosting
CORS configuration
Bucket tagging
versions.explanation: Lifecycle is the common automation.

versions.question: An analytics team reads the same hot dataset many times a day and needs millisecond access with high throughput. Which S3 storage class suits it, and why not the others?
options: S3 Glacier Deep Archive, since it is the cheapest per GB
S3 Standard, since it has no retrieval fee and is built for frequent access
S3 One Zone-IA, since it is the fastest class available
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, since retrievals take only milliseconds
versions.explanation: Frequently accessed data belongs in S3 Standard, the default class; the IA and Glacier classes add retrieval fees or delays.

versions.question: Which storage class do S3 objects get when the upload request does not specify one?
options: S3 Intelligent-Tiering
S3 Standard-IA
S3 Standard
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
versions.explanation: Objects land in S3 Standard, the class for frequently accessed data, unless another class is specified.

versions.question: A tool shows `logs/2026/` as a folder in S3. What is it really?
options: A small bucket nested inside the parent bucket
A shared key prefix; no directory exists
A directory entry that holds its own permissions
An access point defined for that path
versions.explanation: S3 is a flat key-value store.

versions.question: What does the '/' character mean in an S3 key?
options: It creates a nested bucket with separate bucket policies
It switches the object into a different storage class automatically on upload
It marks a separate permission boundary within the bucket
Nothing special to S3; the console treats it as a delimiter
versions.explanation: Keys are flat names.

versions.question: A bucket's versioning is switched to Suspended. What about versions already stored?
options: They are permanently removed once the change is made
They stay stored and remain accessible
Only the newest version is kept and older ones are purged
They are moved to an archive tier automatically
versions.explanation: Suspension only stops new versions.

versions.question: Can versioning be fully disabled once enabled on an S3 bucket?
options: Yes, with a single API call
Yes, but only if the bucket is empty first
No, it can only be suspended
Yes, once replication is turned off
versions.explanation: Enabled buckets can only be suspended.

versions.question: In CloudShell the console Region is eu-west-1. A user creates a file in the home directory and later opens CloudShell in us-west-2. What do they see?
options: The file is present because home storage is global
The file is gone because CloudShell wipes storage after every session
The file is present in S3 automatically
The file isn't there, because storage is separate per Region
versions.explanation: Persistent storage is 1 GB per Region.

versions.question: What defaults apply to commands run in CloudShell?
options: A dedicated service role that is pinned to us-east-1
Your console credentials and the Region currently selected
The credentials of the account's root user
Whatever is stored in ~/.aws/credentials on your laptop
versions.explanation: CloudShell inherits console identity and Region.

versions.question: Which three things can a lifecycle expiration rule delete? (Choose three)
options: Live objects that reach a set age
Noncurrent versions after a number of days
Failed multipart uploads left behind
Objects from a different account's bucket
Idle IAM access keys
EBS snapshots
versions.explanation: Expiration cleans current objects, old versions and incomplete multipart uploads.

versions.question: A bucket accumulates leftover multipart parts and old versions, raising cost. Which three lifecycle actions help? (Choose three)
options: Abort incomplete multipart uploads after some days
Expire noncurrent versions
Expire current log objects after retention
Rotate KMS keys
Delete idle EC2 instances
Remove unused IAM roles
versions.explanation: These are standard S3 lifecycle expiration actions.

versions.question: A site serves the same static assets to users on every continent and tolerates cached copies for a day. Which approach fits?
options: S3 replication to a separate bucket in every Region
CloudFront with a cache TTL set on the content
EFS replicated across several Regions
Route 53 weighted records pointing at several origins
versions.explanation: CloudFront caches at global edge locations, ideal for static content everywhere.

versions.question: Dynamic content must be available with low latency in two specific Regions, as near-real-time read-only copies without caching. What fits best?
options: CloudFront with a long TTL in front of one bucket
S3 Transfer Acceleration enabled on one bucket
Restoring Glacier archives into each Region as needed
S3 Cross-Region Replication into each of the two Regions
versions.explanation: CRR gives read-only replicas per chosen Region without caching.

versions.question: Which target can you NOT select for a Route 53 alias record?
options: An API Gateway endpoint
A Network Load Balancer
An EC2 instance's own DNS hostname
An Elastic Beanstalk environment
versions.explanation: EC2 DNS names are not alias targets.

versions.question: For which of these would you have to use a plain CNAME or A record because alias is unsupported?
options: An S3 static website endpoint in the same account
The auto-assigned hostname of one EC2 server
A Global Accelerator accelerator
A CloudFront web distribution for the site
versions.explanation: Alias supports specific AWS resources, not EC2 names.

versions.question: What is the recommended credential source for code running on EC2 that uploads to S3?
options: Access keys hard-coded in the app configuration
Root user keys placed in environment variables
An instance profile carrying an IAM role
A bucket ACL open to 0.0.0.0/0
versions.explanation: Roles provide temporary credentials automatically.

versions.question: Why attach a role to an EC2 instance rather than storing access keys on it?
options: Roles grant unlimited permissions to the instance
Its credentials are temporary and rotate automatically
Access keys cannot call S3 from EC2 at all
Roles are required before SSH logins are permitted
versions.explanation: Roles avoid long-lived secrets.

versions.question: Generate a pre-signed URL for `s3://docs-bucket/report.pdf` that is valid for 30 minutes.
versions.explanation: `aws s3 presign` takes `--expires-in` in seconds; 30 minutes is 1800.

versions.question: Which command prints a pre-signed download URL for `s3://bkt/file.zip` that expires after 2 hours?
options: aws s3 cp s3://bkt/file.zip - --expires 7200
aws s3api get-object --bucket bkt --key file.zip --expires-in 7200
aws s3 presign s3://bkt/file.zip --expires-in 7200
aws s3 mb s3://bkt/file.zip --expires-in 2h
versions.explanation: `aws s3 presign` with `--expires-in` in seconds; 2 hours is 7200 (the CLI maximum is 604800).

versions.question: A scaled-out web tier across AZs needs a shared writable directory for user uploads. Which storage?
options: A private block volume attached to each server
Amazon EFS, mounted by every instance
The instance store of each server
S3 Glacier mounted as a drive on each server
versions.explanation: EFS is a shared NFS file system with mount targets in each AZ.

versions.question: Which AWS storage can be mounted concurrently by instances in several Availability Zones?
options: A standard EBS volume attached to one instance at a time in one AZ
Instance store volumes on the hosts
An EBS snapshot attached read-only to many hosts
EFS, the regional file system
versions.explanation: EFS is regional and multi-AZ.

versions.question: How do you let CloudFront reach an internal ALB without exposing it to the internet?
options: Place the ALB in a public subnet and open it to 0.0.0.0/0
Assign Elastic IPs to the targets behind it
Create a VPC origin that points at the ALB
Serve the app from a bucket configured for static hosting
versions.explanation: VPC origins keep the origin private.

versions.question: Which resources can be a CloudFront VPC origin? (Choose two)
options: A private Application Load Balancer
An S3 static website endpoint
A private EC2 instance
A Route 53 hosted zone
versions.explanation: VPC origins support private ALB, NLB and EC2.

versions.question: Which three are true of Route 53 alias records? (Choose three)
options: No charge for queries to AWS targets
Allowed at the root domain name
Health of the target can be evaluated
Can target any external website
Require you to set a TTL
Can be of type CNAME
versions.explanation: Aliases are A/AAAA, free to AWS targets and work at the apex.

versions.question: Why choose an alias over a CNAME for example.com pointing to an ALB? (Choose two)
options: CNAME cannot exist at the zone apex
Alias works for any domain on the internet
Alias queries to AWS resources are free
CNAME doesn't support A queries
versions.explanation: Alias works at the apex and costs nothing.

versions.question: An ALB must forward /orders to one fleet and /billing to another. Which feature?
options: Two ALBs joined together with Route 53 records
Sticky sessions turned on for each client
Cross-AZ balancing so that requests spread over all targets in every zone
Path-based listener rules, one target group per path
versions.explanation: ALB supports path, host, header and query routing.

versions.question: Which routing conditions can ALB listener rules use? (Choose two)
options: Host header
Source MAC address
Query string parameter
TCP port of the target
versions.explanation: ALB rules support host, path, header, query string and source IP.

versions.question: Your app uses an AWS SDK and hits throttling. Who handles retries with exponential backoff by default?
options: You, because the SDK never retries on its own
The SDK, automatically
Amazon CloudWatch, for every API call you make
The AWS service quietly retries on your behalf
versions.explanation: SDKs retry automatically; direct HTTP needs custom code.

versions.question: When calling the AWS REST API with plain HTTP requests, how are throttled calls retried?
options: AWS retries them automatically on the server side
CloudTrail resends failed calls
Your own code must implement retry with backoff
The load balancer retries on your behalf
versions.explanation: Only SDKs include built-in retry logic.

versions.question: What is the way to get encryption at rest on an existing unencrypted RDS instance?
options: Modify the instance and tick the encryption box
Snapshot it, copy with encryption on, restore
Create an encrypted read replica and keep that one
Attach a KMS key policy to the existing instance
versions.explanation: Encryption is set at creation; restoring an encrypted snapshot copy is the path.

versions.question: Can an unencrypted RDS primary have an encrypted read replica?
options: Yes, by choosing a KMS key when creating the replica
Yes, but only when the replica is in another Region
No, a replica must match the primary's encryption state
Yes, provided that Multi-AZ is enabled on the primary instance first
versions.explanation: Replicas inherit encryption from the primary.

versions.question: Private instances need outbound-only internet for updates with minimal operations. What do you deploy?
options: A self-managed NAT instance that you patch, size and fail over yourself
An internet gateway plus public IPs on the private instances
A managed NAT Gateway in a public subnet, targeted by the private route table
A NAT Gateway placed inside the private subnet itself
versions.explanation: NAT Gateway is managed and must live in a public subnet.

versions.question: Where must a NAT Gateway be placed?
options: Inside the private subnet it serves
In a public subnet that routes to an internet gateway
In a separate peered VPC that holds shared services
Directly on the internet gateway as an attachment
versions.explanation: It needs a route to the IGW.

versions.question: What should a developer use to authenticate AWS CLI calls from a laptop?
options: Their console password entered when the CLI prompts
Access keys belonging to the account owner, who has full rights
Access keys for their own IAM user, or short-term SSO credentials
A .pem key pair file generated for EC2 logins
versions.explanation: CLI uses access keys or short-term SSO credentials.

versions.question: Which credential type is used for programmatic access to AWS APIs?
options: A console password with a security question
An access key ID with its secret access key
An MFA code entered by itself
A downloaded SSH key file
versions.explanation: Console uses password/MFA; CLI uses access keys.

versions.question: Users are in many countries and the app runs in several Regions. Which Route 53 policy directs each user to the Region with the best measured response time?
options: Geolocation
Latency
Weighted
Failover
versions.explanation: Latency routing uses measured latency between users and Regions; geolocation maps by country and weighted splits by proportion.

versions.question: A user in Germany is sent to a US Region because it answers faster. Which routing policy explains this?
options: Geolocation, which maps countries to endpoints
Simple routing with a single value
Latency-based routing, which ignores geography
Multi-value answer routing
versions.explanation: Latency routing picks the lowest-latency Region, which may not be the closest.

versions.question: Sequence what happens when high load triggers an Auto Scaling scale-out.
items: Load pushes a monitored metric past its threshold
CloudWatch moves the alarm to ALARM
The scaling policy increases desired capacity
The group starts new instances from its launch template
Instances join the load balancer once health checks succeed
versions.explanation: The alarm drives the policy, the ASG launches, and the ELB sends traffic only after health checks pass.

versions.question: In an ASG scale-out, which component directly raises the desired capacity after the alarm fires?
options: The launch template used for new instances
The scaling policy triggered by the alarm
The load balancer receiving the traffic
The AMI baked for the group
versions.explanation: Alarm triggers the policy, which changes desired capacity.

versions.question: Browser-based EC2 Instance Connect can't reach an instance whose security group only allows the office range. What inbound rule is needed?
options: TCP 3389 from the Instance Connect range of that Region
TCP 443 from the Region's published console range
TCP 22 from the Region's EC2_INSTANCE_CONNECT range
ICMP from the console's published address range
versions.explanation: Instance Connect uses SSH, so port 22 from the published EC2_INSTANCE_CONNECT range is needed.

versions.question: Which IAM permission must a user hold to use EC2 Instance Connect?
options: ec2:StartInstances on the target instance
iam:PassRole for the instance profile
ssm:StartSession on the target instance
ec2-instance-connect:SendSSHPublicKey
versions.explanation: The service pushes a temporary public key to the instance using this action.

versions.question: A team needs to send /cart and /checkout requests to different microservices by URL. Which load balancer?
options: Network Load Balancer
An ALB with content-based listener rules
Gateway Load Balancer fronting appliances
Classic Load Balancer with a listener per service
versions.explanation: ALB works at layer 7.

versions.question: Which load balancer operates at layer 4 and handles TCP and UDP traffic?
options: Network Load Balancer (NLB)
An ALB doing HTTP routing
Amazon API Gateway
Amazon CloudFront
versions.explanation: NLB is layer 4.

versions.question: Which three describe CloudFront benefits? (Choose three)
options: Content served from nearby edges
Integrates with Shield and WAF
Origin servers see less traffic
Replicates databases across Regions
Runs EC2 servers for you
Provides block storage
versions.explanation: CDN caching reduces latency and origin load.

versions.question: Which three are reasons to put CloudFront in front of a site? (Choose three)
options: Faster page loads
Absorb attack traffic with Shield/WAF
Reduce origin load via caching
Automatic RDS failover
Managed Kubernetes
Server-side session store
versions.explanation: Edge caching and protection.

versions.question: An EC2 instance in a private subnet calls DynamoDB without using the internet. What is used?
options: A NAT Gateway in a public subnet
A gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB
A route to an internet gateway
A site-to-site VPN connection
versions.explanation: Gateway endpoints exist for S3 and DynamoDB.

versions.question: Which technology provides private access to most AWS services through ENIs in your subnets?
options: A gateway endpoint for S3
A self-managed NAT instance
An interface endpoint (PrivateLink)
VPC peering with a service VPC
versions.explanation: Interface endpoints use PrivateLink.
